# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

I have a complete picture of the repo. Here is the full report.

# 1. Overall repo structure

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                      (python:3.9.2, gunicorn, port 9898)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    (pip package; Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, scikit-learn...)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             (Flask app factory, request timing hooks)
        ├── Controller.py           (HTTP endpoints, per-bank dispatch pipeline)
        ├── BankScripts/            (35 per-bank categorizers: HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/         (shared enrichment stages + regex constants)
```

- **Language/framework**: Python 3.9, Flask web service, pandas-based rule engine. The core pattern everywhere is a list of `[boolean_mask, label]` pairs fed into `np.select(...)` over a transactions DataFrame.
- **Build/run**: `pip3 install -e .` inside `/app/categorizationapp` (see `/app/categorizationapp/setup.py`), served via gunicorn (`/app/Dockerfile:11`), or `python categorizationapp/__init__.py` (dev server, port 9898).
- **Entry points** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`):
  - `POST /categorizeTransaction` (line 69) — payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`. Dispatches to a bank-specific categorizer, then runs shared stages.
  - `POST /recurrentTransactions` (line 55).
- **Git**: single commit `047782b import codebase`.

# 2. Where the enrichment stage lives

The pipeline per bank (see any branch of `Controller.py`, e.g. HDFC at lines 163–186) is:

1. **`categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`** — `BankScripts/<Bank>.py`. Derives `transactionCategory` (CHEQUE_PAID, NEFT, IMPS, UPI, ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION, ...) and extracts raw **`partyName`** (counterparty) from the narration/`description` using per-bank regexes plus splitter helpers.
2. **`purpose()`** — `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — assigns `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN, RENT, ...) and `merchantType`.
3. **`clean_names()`** — `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (1971 lines) — normalizes party names to canonical merchant names.
4. **`internal_payment()`** — `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` — fuzzy-matches partyName to the account holder (fuzzywuzzy, `AppUtil.fuzzy_match`, threshold 75) to flag self-transfers.
5. **`salary_detection()`** — `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py`; optional **`pfm_categorization()`** (`PFMCategorization.py`) and **`simple_description()`** (`SimpleDescription.py`).

Shared plumbing:
- `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` — `clean_input_df` (line 6), splitters `sep_by_dash/sep_by_/sep_by_colon/...` (lines 14–45), `fuzzy_match` (48), `py_extract` regex extractor (61).
- `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — cross-bank keyword regexes (SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REP, CREDIT_CARD, P2P at line 115, MICRO_FIN at 113, ACC_VERIF at line 6...).
- `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (432 lines) — bank-specific narration patterns (HDFC cheque/FT patterns, ICICI/BOI/PNB verification patterns, Union Bank NEFT patterns lines 120–129, etc.).
- `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` / `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` — enum catalogs of labels (e.g. `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` at line 83, `NEFT`=55, `IMPS`=56, `CHEQUE_PAID`=27, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`=57).

# 3. Test fixtures / baseline corpus / test runner

**There are none.** The repo contains 52 files, all production code:
- No `tests/`, no `*test*` files (glob returned nothing), no CSV/JSON/YAML fixtures anywhere, no pytest/tox/CI config, no README/Makefile.
- `setup.py` declares no test dependencies; git history is a single "import codebase" commit.
- The only way to exercise the code today is to POST a transactions payload to `/categorizeTransaction`. If you need a labelled baseline corpus of statement narrations, it would have to be created — the regexes in `BankRegexConstants.py`/`RegexConstants.py` are effectively the fossilized record of past narrations.

# 4. The four specific behaviours

### a) Cheque debits (CHQ)
Every bank script has a CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT rule pair keyed on `type` DEBIT/CREDIT. Key sites:
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:71` — `"\bCHQ\b|^I/W CHQ RETURN|cheque"` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; line 73 CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; line 74 `Chq Paid|CHQ COLL|CHEQ PAID` → CHEQUE_PAID; line 50 `CASH CHEQUE` → `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`; line 100 infers CHEQUE_DEPOSIT from a 16-char numeric `remark`.
- `BankScripts/Kotak.py:64-67` — `\bCLG\b|\bMICR\b|\bCHQ\b` CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, DEBIT→CHEQUE_PAID; also 3–5 digit `remark` = cheque number.
- `BankScripts/Central.py:45-46`, `BankScripts/BOB.py:68-69`, `BankScripts/YES.py:45-46`, `BankScripts/Canara.py:70-71`, `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:50`, `BankScripts/Syndicate.py:52-53`, `BankScripts/KarurVyasa.py:48`, `BankScripts/AuSmallFinanceBank.py:38`, `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:65`.
- Cheque **counterparty extraction** (payee name from CHQ narration): `HDFC.py:188-197` using `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` from `BankRegexConstants.py:81-90`; `Central.py:73-74`; `Canara.py:164-166`; `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:78`; `Axis.py:145` (`BRN-CLG-CHQ PAID TO <name>`); `Citi.py:119,128,143`.
- Related: `CHEQUE_RETURN`/`CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY` rules (e.g. `HDFC.py:30,69-72`; `Citi.py:30`) and bounce subcategorization in `Purpose.py:145-147` (`TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`/`INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`).

### b) MICR clearing narrations, e.g. `"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR"`
- **HDFC** is the main MICR handler. Patterns in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:81-90`:
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1` (81): `"MICR 1 CLG - NO :|- - MICR CLG -|- MICR - MICR CLG -|..."`
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN2` (82): `"CHQ DEP - MICR [0-9] CLEARING|MICR CLG - [A-Z]+ : |..."`
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN3` (83): `"MICR CLG - [A-Z]+"`
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` (86): `"Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS"`
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN10` (90): `"CHQ DEP - .* - MICR.*:(.*):"`
  These are applied for name extraction in `BankScripts/HDFC.py:188-197`; additionally `HDFC.py:163` splits any `CHQ PAID-` narration with `sep_by_dash(desc,3,4)`, and `HDFC.py:260` blanks partyName if it still equals `"Micr Clg"`/`"Chq Paid"` (i.e. structural tokens must never leak as a counterparty).
  - Note: HDFC's `remark` heuristic for cheques is line 100 (`^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` MICR-style cheque number).
- **Central Bank** handles the exact shape `CHQ PAID-<clearing>-<NAME>`: `BankScripts/Central.py:73` extracts via `"PAID (.*) -"`, and line 74 `CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(desc,2,3)` → for `"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR"` this yields **"RAVI KUMAR"**. Category comes from line 45 (`...|CHQ PAID|\bCHQ\b` + DEBIT → CHEQUE_PAID).
- **Canara**: `Canara.py:164` (`Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` → dash tokens 2:3), `Canara.py:165` (`^CHQ PAID-` → dash tokens 1:2).
- Other MICR references: `Citi.py:30` (`RETURN OF MICR CLG CHQ` → CHEQUE_RETURN), `BankOfMaharashtra.py:65` (`MICR CLG` credit → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT), `Kotak.py:64,66` (`\bMICR\b`), `BOB.py:68-69` (`MICR INWD CLG`), and `BankRegexConstants.py:314-317` (`CHQ_PATTERN1..4` = `"MICR INWARD..."` — used by StandardCharted).

### c) NEFT credits
- Detection per bank (all direction-agnostic, `type` distinguishes credit/debit): `HDFC.py:60` (`NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-` — `NEFT CR-` is the credit form), `ICICI.py:64` (`^NEFT|BIL/NEFT/|^INF/NEFT/`), `SBI.py:55`, `Axis.py:49`, `Kotak.py:49` (`NEFTINW` = inward), `BOB.py:57`, `PNB.py:52`, `Central.py:43`, `Federal.py:34`, `Indusind.py:19`, `IDBI.py:43`, plus ~20 more (full list found at `BankScripts/*` — every script has one NEFT rule).
- NEFT **counterparty (remitter/beneficiary) extraction**:
  - `HDFC.py:157-161` — `^NEFT CR-<UTR>-<7+digits>-` → dash tokens 3:4; `^NEFT [CD]R-<IFSC11>-...` → tokens 2:4; generic `^IMPS-|^NEFT CR` → tokens 2:3; `HDFC.py:226` blanks garbage numeric names.
  - `BankOfMaharashtra.py:122-142` — ~20 narration variants (`NEFT <UTR> <NAME> MAHB...`), plus cleanup at line 203.
  - Union Bank patterns `UB_NEFT_1..8_UNION` in `BankRegexConstants.py:120-127` (e.g. `^NEFT:IBUSER-(.*) SAA[0-9]+`), used in `UnionBank.py`.
  - `IDBI.py:91-97`, `ICICI.py:157-158`, `SBI.py:120-122`, `Indusind.py:239-251`, `Central.py:66,71-72`.
- `NEFT_RETURN` and `NEFT_CHARGES` categories: `HDFC.py:28`, enums at `TransactionCategoryEnums.py:64,139`.

### d) IMPS / instant P2P credits
- Detection: `HDFC.py:59` (`IMPS-`), `ICICI.py:62` (`^MMT/IMPS`), `SBI.py:54` (`IMPS|I M P S`), `Axis.py:48` (`^IMPS/`), `Kotak.py:43,48` (note `^IMPS from|^Received from` credit narrations), `Indusind.py:49` (`^IMPS|IMPS/P2A|IMPS / P2A|MPSP2...`), `BankOfMaharashtra.py:59`, `Paytm.py:29`, etc.
- **P2A (person-to-account, i.e. P2P) narration parsing** — the `IMPS/P2A/` token appears in:
  - `BOB.py:130-135` (progressive fallbacks: `IMPS/P2A/` with masked account `X{4,}` etc. → slash tokens 3:4 or 4:5), cleanup at 147, 152.
  - `StandardCharted.py:124-134, 181-182` (extracts sender name after IFSC/UTR in `Inward Credit - IMPS IMPS/P2A ...`).
  - `Indusind.py:198-204` (`IMPSP2A...INWD####INET/MOB/BRC` inward-credit variants), `UCO.py:69`, `Axis.py:119-122`, `Indian.py:65` (`BY TRANSFER /IMPS/P2A/(.*) TRANSFER FROM`), `Central.py:69-70` (`BY TRANSFER/IMPSP2A<digits> <NAME>`), `Karnataka.py:62`, `PNB.py:94`, `DCB.py:77-78` (`IMPSIW:P2A FRM (<name>)/`), `SouthIndian.py:65-67`, `BankOfMaharashtra.py:204-207`.
  - SBI-specific IMPS patterns `SBI_IMPS_1..3` at `BankRegexConstants.py:60-62`, applied in `SBI.py:149-152,185`.
  - `IMPS_REVERSAL`/`IMPS_CHARGES`: `HDFC.py:23,34`; enums `TransactionCategoryEnums.py:120-121`.
  - (Unrelated homonym: `P2P` in `RegexConstants.py:115` means P2P-NBFC lenders, used in `Purpose.py:190-191` for merchantType, not IMPS.)

### e) Account-verification / penny-drop deposits
Category label: `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` (`TransactionCategoryEnums.py:83`). The rule is universally "verification-looking narration AND amount ≈ ₹1":
- Shared regexes in `BankRegexConstants.py`: `BANK_VER` (line 327: `"PennyD rop|...|pennydrop|valida|ny\s?drop..."`), `BANK_VER_ICICI` (69), `BANK_VER_HD` (75), `BANK_VER_BOI` (110), `ACC_VERI_UNION` (116), `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` (133), `ACC_VERI_SCB` (431); plus `ACC_VERIF` in `RegexConstants.py:6` (`"...pennyd|...|/bene|/bav|BANK DETAILS VALID"`).
- Per-bank rules (all early in each script so verification wins before NEFT/IMPS rules):
  - `HDFC.py:13` — `BANK_VER` & `amount < 2`.
  - `ICICI.py:11` — `BANK_VER_ICICI` & `amount ∈ {1,-1}` & not `RVSL`.
  - `SBI.py:12` — `ACC_VERIF` & CREDIT & `amount == 1`.
  - `Paytm.py:15-16` — includes **`IMPS` & amount==1 & CREDIT → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`** (the pure penny-drop-via-IMPS case).
  - `Axis.py:24-26` — regex match; `MANDATE` & amount 1; and blanket **any ₹1 CREDIT** → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION; `Axis.py:123` still extracts the party for verification IMPS.
  - `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` (any ₹1 CREDIT), `Indusind.py:29-31` (₹1 DEBIT), `Kotak.py:13-14` (`^Received from <NAME>` & ₹1 CREDIT), `Canara.py:19` (`amount < 1`), `RBL.py:15`, `PNB.py:12`, `BOI.py:12`, `BOB.py:12`, `IDFC.py:12`, `IDBI.py:12`, `Karnataka.py:12`, `UnionBank.py:12`, `Central.py:12`, `Andhra.py:12`, `YES.py:14`, `Syndicate.py:12`, `StandardCharted.py:13`, `SouthIndian.py:12`, `TamilnadMerchantile.py:13`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12`.
- Downstream interaction: `Purpose.py:165` reclassifies ₹1 "LOAN" subcategory txns to ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION; `Purpose.py:173` strips subcategory for VERIFICATION txns; `SalaryDetection.py:205` excludes them from salary logic; `IDFC.py:71-72` and `ICICI.py:166-167` skip name extraction when category is ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION; `SimpleDescription.py:8` includes it in the human-readable description list.

**Key caveat for your work**: all logic is order-sensitive `np.select` (first matching rule wins), per-bank, regex-only — and there is zero test coverage, so any regression harness/baseline corpus of labelled narrations (e.g. `"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR"` → CHEQUE_PAID / "Ravi Kumar") would be net-new.

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/app/categorizationapp")

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.AppUtil import clean_input_df
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.InternalPayment import internal_payment
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.SalaryDetection import salary_detection
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.PNB import categorize_PNB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Canara import categorize_Canara_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Bandhan import categorize_Bandhan_transactions


def full(fn, bank, rows, accountType="SAVING", accountHolder="SURESH PATEL"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "remark", "amount", "balanceAfterTransaction", "type"])
    # emulate Controller payload columns
    df["date"] = pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=len(df), freq="D").strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    df = clean_input_df(df)
    df = fn(df, accountType)
    df = purpose(df, accountType)
    df = clean_names(df, accountType, bank)
    df = internal_payment(df, accountHolder, bank, accountType)
    res = salary_detection(df)
    df = df if res is None else res
    return df[["description", "type", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]]


print("#### PNB end-to-end")
print(full(categorize_PNB_transactions, "PNB", [
    ["123456",          "123456", 25000, 1e5, "DEBIT"],
    ["NEFT RAVI KUMAR", "",       52000, 1e5, "CREDIT"],
]).to_string(index=False))

print("#### CANARA end-to-end")
print(full(categorize_Canara_transactions, "CANARA", [
    ["CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR", "", 45000, 1e5, "DEBIT"],
    ["Account validation",           "", 1,     1e5, "CREDIT"],
]).to_string(index=False))

print("#### BANDHAN end-to-end")
print(full(categorize_Bandhan_transactions, "BANDHAN", [
    ["DEPOSIT,IMPS/P2A/512912345678/RAVI KUMAR", "", 15000, 1e5, "CREDIT"],
]).to_string(index=False))

steps.message:
All five RC 2.14 findings are traced to root cause and fixed. Three files changed, five minimal edits.

## Root causes and fixes

**F-1 — bare cheque-number note debited as TRANSFER** → `BankScripts/PNB.py:60`
The debit-side rule accepted only exactly 5 digits in the remark (`^[0-9]{5}$`) while its credit twin on the very next line accepts `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. A 6-digit cheque number with nothing else beside it matched no rule and fell to the `TRANSFER` default. Widened the debit rule to `^[0-9]{5,6}$` to match the credit side.

**F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` returns the clearing tag** → `BankScripts/Canara.py:165`
The generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule takes dash-token 1, which for this layout is the internal tag `MICR CLG` (surfacing as "Micr Clg"). The sibling rule for `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` correctly takes token 2. Added a dedicated `^CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` rule (token 2:3) ahead of the generic one; `CHQ PAID-<NAME>` narrations still hit the generic rule unchanged.

**F-3 — plain NEFT credits with blank counterparty** → `BankScripts/PNB.py:110`
The catch-all for `^NEFT ` narrations called `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` — the pattern has a single capture group (index 0), so `.get(1)` returns `None` and `py_extract` yields `""` for *every* matching row. That's why exactly the "plain" layout went blank while `NEFT_IN:`, `NEFT-IB-OW/`, etc. kept resolving. Changed `index=1` → `index=0`.

**F-4 — P2P IMPS credit shows the bare RRN** → `BankScripts/Bandhan.py:61`
The generic IMPS rule takes slash-token 2. For `…IMPS/P2A/<RRN>/<SENDER>` the extra `P2A` segment shifts the name right by one, so token 2 is the 12-digit reference — and Bandhan has no numeric-name cleanup, so it surfaced verbatim. Added an `IMPS/P2A/` rule (token 3:4) ahead of the generic rule; non-P2A layouts (`IMPS/<ref>/<name>`, space-broken `I M P S /`) are untouched.

**F-5 — ₹1 penny-drop filed as TRANSFER** → `BankScripts/Canara.py:19`
The verification rule required `amount.lt(1)`, which excludes exactly the standard one-rupee confirmation credit (every other bank uses `lt(2)` / `eq(1)` / `isin([1,-1])`). Changed to `amount.le(1)` — a strict superset of the old condition, so everything it previously matched still matches, plus the ₹1 case.

## Verification
- Built a deterministic offline harness that replays each finding's narration form plus neighbouring layouts through the bank categorizers (and through the full `purpose → clean_names → internal_payment` chain): all five regressed forms now derive their baseline category/name (e.g. `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → `CHEQUE_PAID` / "Ravi Kumar"; `NEFT RAVI KUMAR` credit → `NEFT` / "Ravi Kumar"; P2A credit → `IMPS` / "Ravi Kumar"; ₹1 verification credit → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`; 6-digit remark debit → `CHEQUE_PAID`).
- Ran a before/after sweep of ~35 representative narrations across the three touched banks against the original code: the diff contains only the five intended rows — 5-digit remarks, 7/4-digit remarks, `CHQ PAID-<NAME>`, `Home Clearing`, non-P2A IMPS, all other NEFT layouts, sub-rupee verification, ordinary deposits/transfers all reproduce their previous output exactly.

One note for engineering, outside this ticket's scope (left untouched since acceptance forbids moving anything unlisted): `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:100` is a malformed rule row (`&` joins the condition and the choice into a single element), which is worth a look in a future pass.
